subject: Performance sprint kickoff & cost ops scope

Subject: Performance sprint kickoff & cost ops scope

Hi Sasha —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation I'd like to propose a focused 2–3 week \"performance sprint\" to lock in latency and unit-cost targets before we move to a wider rollout. The sprint scope would cover:

- Batching and request shaping (target: preserve p95 latency while increasing agg throughput)
- Prefix/KV caching policy for your conversational flows
- Quantization profile testing (CPU/GPU fallbacks and near-lossless configs)
- Smart routing policy (primary model vs. cheaper variant under load)

Proposed outcomes by end of sprint:
- Baseline cost/latency report with token-level breakdowns
- Recommended quant profile per endpoint and a canary plan
- Updated mutual action plan (MAP) with test windows and rollback points

I've attached a short kickoff deck and a draft MAP worksheet to this email. For next steps: can you share a week-long sample of production traffic (anonymized) and a target p95 SLO you want us to optimize for? Also please confirm calendar availability for a 45-minute kick off on Tue/Wed next week.

Attachments: kickoff-deck.pdf (PDF, 2.4MB), mutual-action-plan.xlsx (Excel, 48KB)

Best,
Grace O'Connor

Grace —

Thanks, this looks solid. A couple quick constraints from our side:

- Data: traffic will be HIPAA-adjacent (we'll anonymize payloads before sharing).
- Latency SLO: 150ms p95 for inference (including network overhead) for our chat endpoint.
- Budget: we need to stay within roughly $0.0035 per request for peak traffic (we can provide monthly spend limits).

I can share an anonymized trace dump (JSON) and a small CSV of request sizes tomorrow. For the kickoff, Wed Aug 4 at 10:00am PT works for me. Would like a line item in the MAP that specifies canary rollback criteria (error spike >2x baseline or p95 >250ms for 5m).

—Sasha

Subject: Re: Performance sprint kickoff & cost ops scope

Folks — quick tech note before the kickoff:

If AtlasAI's target is 150ms p95, we'll want to prioritize a low-latency pathway for the small-chat flows and a deferred pathway for longer fulllength generations. Practical starting points:

- Quantization: bring q4_k_mixed and q8_0 candidates into the sprint. q4_k_mixed gives ~2.4x cost reduction with typically <2% eval delta on summarization tasks; q8_0 is safer for shorter context.
- Batching: client-side micro-batching (100–200ms window) + dynamic server batching tuned to keep p95 under SLO. We'll test windows of 50ms / 100ms / 200ms in three canary waves.
- Caching: prefix cache keyed by conversation ID + last-system-prompt hash. We'll push a conservative TTL (30s) during spike windows, then relax if hit rates are low.

I'll attach a small synthetic traffic sample and a quick quant-profiles.json that maps the profiles we should run in week 1. If Sasha can provide real traffic characteristics (seq length, tokens per call, % streaming vs non-streaming) we can tailor the batches.

Attachment: traffic-sample.csv (CSV, 12KB), quant-profiles.json (5KB)

Ben
